prerequisites: It is discouraged to choose this course without taking, or having previously taken, the rest of the subjects in the “Robotic Systems” module.

learning_outcomes.text: Conduct research, development, and innovation in products, processes, and methods.
Apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within multidisciplinary contexts related to their field of study.
Communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Develop learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
Apply the acquired knowledge in the design and implementation of a robotic system.
Be able to work in a group through effective communication.
Be able to define, refocus, and meet the system design specifications.
Be able to respond to problems or unforeseen events that arise during development.
Present and orally defend the project carried out.

assessment_rules: The final project will be proposed by the course professors and developed in successive stages. It will evaluate its scope, technical difficulty, and resources used. Each student will submit a written document and give an oral presentation with a Q&A session. The quality of the written document, oral presentation, ability to answer questions, and the scope and relevance of the results presented will be assessed, along with the individual involvement of each group member. Extraordinary calls and differentiated evaluation will follow the same assessment system (50% project + 50% presentation).
